reason: Zero external dependencies required; portable across IDEs

decision: Use Layered Memory Engine with Confidence Classification
reason: Distinguish Known facts from Assumed vs Unknown hypotheses

decision: Scope working/session/project memory to the bound project
reason: One Core governs many repositories. A single global project.json accumulated every repo's stack facts, so an agent could read another project's frameworks as though they described the current one. Discovered when init seeded scratch-project facts into the real Core store.
alternatives: Project key field on each fact with reader-side filtering
Registry of per-project files under CoreSentinel/memory/projects/
Leave global and document the limitation
chosen: Project-scoped layers resolve to <project>/.coresentinel/memory via upward .coresentinel/config.json discovery, falling back to the Core store when unbound

decision: Project-to-longterm memory promotion requires an explicit transferable mark
reason: A project-scoped fact is a claim about one codebase by definition. Auto-promoting high-confidence project facts into the shared Core would leak one repository's stack into every repository the Core governs - the exact failure the project/core scoping split exists to prevent.
alternatives: Fully automatic promotion on confidence alone
Promote only facts sourced from the Core
chosen: Opt-in: project to longterm needs confidence >= 0.95, 14+ days age AND an explicit transferable flag; session to project stays automatic at >= 0.90 because both are project-scoped

decision: Standing Rule 7 resolves the shell from the host OS instead of assuming Windows
reason: The rule was wrong for 100 percent of commands in the 2026-08-15 darwin session: python is absent, zsh is the shell, && is required. A rule agents must ignore to function is worse than no rule, because it also teaches them the rulebook is optional. Deleting it loses the genuine Windows constraints.
chosen: Rule 7 is now platform-conditional: resolve the host OS at session start, then take the Windows branch (PowerShell 5.1, python, no &&) or the macOS/Linux branch (zsh/bash, python3, && permitted). The Windows constraints are preserved verbatim.
alternatives: Leave the rule unconditional and let agents silently ignore it on Unix; delete the rule entirely
problem: Standing Rule 7 mandated PowerShell 5.1, 'python never python3', and no && for all agents on all projects, unconditionally.
evidence: EVO-004; darwin 24.6.0 session 2026-08-15; corroborated by the 2026-08-10 OneDrive HOME/Desktop and sed Windows-path anti-patterns in 55-self-evolution.md
